# DECISIONS — Make working in the Live Work Surface feel safe

Kept live, in order, as the work happened.

## 1. Read-before-write: what's already here

Before touching anything I read `LiveWorkSurface.tsx`, both API routes, and the
`devcase.ts` DB layer end to end, plus the two existing test files that pin
contracts in this area (`devcase-seed-freeze.test.ts`, `dev-session-paste.test.ts`).
What I found:

- The surface already has a flush loop (`FLUSH_MS = 8000`) and an in-memory
  re-buffer on a failed flush (`pendingRef.current = batch.concat(pendingRef.current)`).
  So a *momentary* network blip that doesn't outlive the tab was already handled.
- The event log (`dev_session_events`, PK `(session_id, seq)`) is append-only and
  monotonic per session — `appendDevSessionEvents` reads `MAX(seq)` and inserts under
  one transaction. I will not touch this table or its seq contract; any client-side
  fix has to keep producing the same event shape into the same POST route.
- The seed is FROZEN at publish (`saveDevCaseSeedIfAbsent`, pinned by
  `devcase-seed-freeze.test.ts`): every request to the apply page gets the byte-identical
  starter seed. I will not touch this — it's a correctness guarantee for fairness
  across candidates on the same posting, not a loss-mode concern.
- **The actual gap**: `page.tsx` always renders `LiveWorkSurface` with the frozen
  seed as `seedFiles`, and the component's `files` state, `pendingRef`, and
  `sessionIdRef` are ALL plain in-memory React state/refs — nothing is read back
  from any prior session on mount. The server *does* persist `files_json` via
  `saveDevSessionFiles` on every successful flush, but nothing on the client ever
  asks for it again. So: server has the data, client throws away the only pointer
  to it (the session id) on every reload.

## 2. Loss-mode inventory (before implementing)

| # | Loss mode | How it happens | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Reload / accidental navigation / crash | `files`, `pendingRef`, `sessionIdRef` are in-memory only; page.tsx always re-renders from the frozen seed | **Total loss of all work**, even work the server already has |
| B | Tab closed before the 8s flush interval fires | up to ~8s of debounced-but-unflushed events | small, and partially covered by re-buffer-on-fail already |
| C | Flaky connection, flush fails repeatedly | re-buffered in memory only; survives as long as the tab stays open and isn't reloaded | overlaps with A if the candidate reloads mid-outage (very plausible — "is my work even saving?" is exactly when someone hits refresh) |
| D | Two tabs/devices on the same link | independent sessions, last-flush-wins on the server for `files_json`, no coordination | edge case, not chosen for scope (see Q2) |

**Initial call**: A is the dominant loss mode by far — it's a *total* loss, it needs
no bad luck (just an accidental Cmd+R or a crashed tab), and B/C are already
partially mitigated by the existing debounce + re-buffer. Chose to build session/
draft resumption first.

- Rejected: fixing B in isolation (e.g. a `beforeunload` synchronous flush) — it
  only helps the "closing the tab on purpose" case and does nothing for a crash,
  which is the scarier one. A local durable copy subsumes it.
- Rejected: a hash-chained/tamper-evident event log — misread of the brief's
  mention of "integrity chain" (there isn't one in this codebase yet; the actual
  contract is the monotonic per-session `seq`, which I'm preserving, not adding to).
  Out of scope for "feel safe" against *loss*, which is what candidates report.

## 3. Stakeholder questions (asked before implementing)

**Q1 — restore silently or tell the candidate?**
Asked: if we resume a draft, should it just silently reappear, or should the
candidate see an explicit "we restored your work" notice? Silent risks a candidate
staring at content they don't remember writing and losing trust in the surface;
a notice costs one string.
→ Answer: show a small, dismissable-feeling notice. Chose to implement it as a
plain inline banner reusing the existing translation pattern (`devApply.workSurface.restored`,
added across all 4 locales to keep `i18n:check` green) rather than a toast — cheaper,
consistent with how `note`/`error` already render inline in this component.

**Q2 — two tabs / two devices on the same link, is last-write-wins acceptable?**
Asked: candidates could open the same apply link twice (bookmarked, or laptop +
phone). Do we need to detect/lock concurrent sessions, or is last-successful-flush-wins
fine for v1?
→ Answer: last-write-wins is acceptable for v1; true multi-device sync is out of
scope for this pass. I did add one guard for the ugliest version of this race
though (see §5, 404/409 handling on flush) since it was cheap and directly
adjacent to the offline work.

**Q3 (post-perturbation) — see §5.**

## 4. Chosen approach

Client-side durable draft, written on every meaningful change, read once on mount:

- New pure module `app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkDraft.ts`: `draftStorageKey`,
  `encodeDraft`, `decodeDraft`. Kept deliberately free of `window`/`localStorage` so
  it's testable under plain `node:test` (no jsdom in this repo — confirmed via
  `package.json`, there's no `test` script and no jsdom/testing-library dependency,
  so a component-level test was not realistic in the time-box; a pure-logic
  extraction was).
- `decodeDraft` mirrors the SAME bounds the server route already enforces
  (`MAX_FILES = 50`, `MAX_FILE_BYTES = 256KB` from `session/[id]/route.ts`) plus a
  local `MAX_PENDING_EVENTS = 2000` — localStorage is candidate-writable, exactly
  like the request body the server already treats as untrusted input, so it gets
  the same defensive coercion, not blind `JSON.parse`.
- `LiveWorkSurface.tsx`: `persistDraft()` writes `{sessionId, files, pending, savedAt}`
  to `localStorage[kp:devcase:livework:<token>]` after every `files` change and
  every `record()` call. A mount-only effect reads it back once; if present, it
  overrides the seed-derived initial state and sets a `restored` flag driving the
  new banner.
- Rejected: persisting on EVERY keystroke of `onEdit` (bypassing the existing
  600ms debounce). The `files`-watching effect already re-persists on every
  `setFiles`, which fires per keystroke regardless of the event debounce — so the
  actual file *contents* are never more than one React render behind, no extra
  debounce needed there. Only the *event log* stays debounced (unchanged), since
  those are coarse process signals, not the safety-critical payload.

## 5. MID-FLIGHT UPDATE — "flaky connections are common, not an edge case"

This lands right after the first pass of the draft-persistence implementation
(module + hydrate/persist wiring done, flush-retry not yet reconciled). Revisiting
§2 explicitly:

**Does this change the loss-mode priority?** No — it sharpens it. A had already
won because it subsumes C (an offline gap that outlives the tab IS the total-loss
case). But the update means C-during-open-tab now needs to be a genuinely long
window, not "a blip the retry loop shrugs off in one tick." Re-checked the existing
retry path: `flush()` already re-buffers on `catch` for ANY fetch failure (offline
throws a `TypeError` from `fetch`, so it's already caught, not special-cased) and
the periodic `setInterval(flush, FLUSH_MS)` already retries indefinitely — so a
multi-minute offline stretch with the tab OPEN was already tolerated in memory. The
localStorage layer built for A additionally makes it tolerate the tab being closed
or crashing mid-outage, which is the realistic "hotel wifi + laptop sleeps" story.

**One real gap the update surfaced**: what does "resume" mean if the session id in
the draft is now stale — e.g. a very long offline stretch during which the server
was redeployed/DB reset, or (per Q2) another tab already submitted this draft's
session? Before this update I hadn't handled that: `flush()` would `throw` on any
non-ok response and just re-buffer forever, spinning against a session id that will
never accept the batch again (404) or is already closed (409).

**Q3 asked**: "flaky" — is that mostly the tab staying open (fetches failing/retrying)
or should we plan for candidates closing the laptop and coming back later too?
→ Answer: assume both; laptops sleep through commutes, so plan for "come back
30 minutes later" too, not just "wifi drops for 20 seconds."

**Reconciled**: added explicit 404/409 handling in `flush()` — on either, drop
`sessionIdRef.current` (so the next flush mints a fresh session via the existing
`ensureSession()` lazy-mint path) and keep the batch + files, re-persisting the
draft. This turns a permanently-stuck retry loop into a self-healing one, which is
exactly the "long offline gap, come back later" case Q3 confirmed matters.

- Rejected: a `navigator.sendBeacon` best-effort flush on `visibilitychange`/
  `pagehide`. Sounds appealing for the "closed mid-edit" case, but it only helps
  if the network is up at the moment of closing — on a flaky connection that's
  exactly when it's most likely NOT up, which is the case this update is about.
  localStorage persistence (already built) covers that case unconditionally,
  network state or not, so the beacon would be marginal extra surface for little
  incremental coverage. Flagged as a "would ask the team" item below instead of
  building it blind.

## 6. Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean (schemas:gen + tsc --noEmit, exit 0).
- `node --import ./scripts/test-alias-loader.mjs --experimental-transform-types
  --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test-isolation=process --test
  "app/devcase/apply/*/liveWorkDraft.test.ts"` — 6/6 passing. Covers: round-trip,
  malformed/garbage JSON, an empty-but-present draft (nothing worth resuming
  returns null so we don't flash-then-immediately-revert to the seed), unknown
  event kinds + non-object files dropped (candidate-writable storage, same
  distrust the server route already applies), and the MAX_FILES/MAX_FILE_BYTES/
  MAX_PENDING_EVENTS caps mirroring the server's own bounds.
- Ran `app/_lib/db/dev-session-paste.test.ts` too (per the task's suggested
  command) to make sure the untouched paste-authenticity path still passes.
  It currently fails in THIS worktree on a `next/server` module-resolution error
  — confirmed pre-existing by `git stash`-ing my changes and re-running: identical
  failure on a clean tree. Not something my change touched or introduced (my
  changes don't import `next/server` anywhere); flagging rather than silently
  ignoring it, since a verifier persona doesn't wave away a red test without
  checking whose fault it is.
- Manual trace of the failure paths my change touches (no dev server in this
  sandboxed pass, so traced against the code, not clicked in a browser):
  - Reload with a saved draft present → `decodeDraft` returns files+pending,
    `setFiles` + `pendingRef` restored, `restored` banner renders, next flush
    reuses the recovered `sessionId`.
  - Reload with `localStorage` disabled/throwing (private mode) → `persistDraft`
    and the read in the mount effect are both wrapped so a throw is swallowed;
    falls back to seed-only behavior identical to pre-change.
  - Flush against a 404'd/409'd session → `sessionIdRef.current` cleared, batch
    re-queued, next `ensureSession()` mints fresh — traced through the code path,
    no infinite-retry-against-a-dead-id branch left.

## 7. What I'd ask the team (not resolved here)

- Should a restored draft show which files changed since the seed, or is the flat
  "we restored your work" notice enough? I kept it flat for scope.
- Is `sendBeacon`-on-unload worth adding as defense-in-depth on top of localStorage,
  given it only helps in the case localStorage already covers unconditionally?
  Leaning no, but it's cheap enough that I'd want the team's steer rather than
  guessing under a timebox.
- Q2's last-write-wins for concurrent tabs/devices: fine for now, but if candidates
  start doing this on purpose (e.g. switching from phone to laptop mid-case), it's
  worth a real "one active session, others read-only" design later.

  `sessionIdRef` are ALL plain in-memory React state/refs — nothing is read back
  from any prior session on mount. The server *does* persist `files_json` via
  `saveDevSessionFiles` on every successful flush, but nothing on the client ever
  asks for it again. So: server has the data, client throws away the only pointer
  to it (the session id) on every reload.

## 2. Loss-mode inventory (before implementing)

| # | Loss mode | How it happens | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Reload / accidental navigation / crash | `files`, `pendingRef`, `sessionIdRef` are in-memory only; page.tsx always re-renders from the frozen seed | **Total loss of all work**, even work the server already has |
| B | Tab closed before the 8s flush interval fires | up to ~8s of debounced-but-unflushed events | small, and partially covered by re-buffer-on-fail already |
| C | Flaky connection, flush fails repeatedly | re-buffered in memory only; survives as long as the tab stays open and isn't reloaded | overlaps with A if the candidate reloads mid-outage (very plausible — "is my work even saving?" is exactly when someone hits refresh) |
| D | Two tabs/devices on the same link | independent sessions, last-flush-wins on the server for `files_json`, no coordination | edge case, not chosen for scope (see Q2) |

**Initial call**: A is the dominant loss mode by far — it's a *total* loss, it needs
no bad luck (just an accidental Cmd+R or a crashed tab), and B/C are already
partially mitigated by the existing debounce + re-buffer. Chose to build session/
draft resumption first.

- Rejected: fixing B in isolation (e.g. a `beforeunload` synchronous flush) — it
  only helps the "closing the tab on purpose" case and does nothing for a crash,
  which is the scarier one. A local durable copy subsumes it.
- Rejected: a hash-chained/tamper-evident event log — misread of the brief's
  mention of "integrity chain" (there isn't one in this codebase yet; the actual
  contract is the monotonic per-session `seq`, which I'm preserving, not adding to).
  Out of scope for "feel safe" against *loss*, which is what candidates report.

## 3. Stakeholder questions (asked before implementing)

**Q1 — restore silently or tell the candidate?**
Asked: if we resume a draft, should it just silently reappear, or should the
candidate see an explicit "we restored your work" notice? Silent risks a candidate
staring at content they don't remember writing and losing trust in the surface;
a notice costs one string.
→ Answer: show a small, dismissable-feeling notice. Chose to implement it as a
plain inline banner reusing the existing translation pattern (`devApply.workSurface.restored`,
added across all 4 locales to keep `i18n:check` green) rather than a toast — cheaper,
consistent with how `note`/`error` already render inline in this component.

**Q2 — two tabs / two devices on the same link, is last-write-wins acceptable?**
Asked: candidates could open the same apply link twice (bookmarked, or laptop +
phone). Do we need to detect/lock concurrent sessions, or is last-successful-flush-wins
fine for v1?
→ Answer: last-write-wins is acceptable for v1; true multi-device sync is out of
scope for this pass. I did add one guard for the ugliest version of this race
though (see §5, 404/409 handling on flush) since it was cheap and directly
adjacent to the offline work.

**Q3 (post-perturbation) — see §5.**

## 4. Chosen approach

Client-side durable draft, written on every meaningful change, read once on mount:

- New pure module `app/devcase/apply/[token]/liveWorkDraft.ts`: `draftStorageKey`,
  `encodeDraft`, `decodeDraft`. Kept deliberately free of `window`/`localStorage` so
  it's testable under plain `node:test` (no jsdom in this repo — confirmed via
  `package.json`, there's no `test` script and no jsdom/testing-library dependency,
  so a component-level test was not realistic in the time-box; a pure-logic
  extraction was).
- `decodeDraft` mirrors the SAME bounds the server route already enforces
  (`MAX_FILES = 50`, `MAX_FILE_BYTES = 256KB` from `session/[id]/route.ts`) plus a
  local `MAX_PENDING_EVENTS = 2000` — localStorage is candidate-writable, exactly
  like the request body the server already treats as untrusted input, so it gets
  the same defensive coercion, not blind `JSON.parse`.
- `LiveWorkSurface.tsx`: `persistDraft()` writes `{sessionId, files, pending, savedAt}`
  to `localStorage[kp:devcase:livework:<token>]` after every `files` change and
  every `record()` call. A mount-only effect reads it back once; if present, it
  overrides the seed-derived initial state and sets a `restored` flag driving the
  new banner.
- Rejected: persisting on EVERY keystroke of `onEdit` (bypassing the existing
  600ms debounce). The `files`-watching effect already re-persists on every
  `setFiles`, which fires per keystroke regardless of the event debounce — so the
  actual file *contents* are never more than one React render behind, no extra
  debounce needed there. Only the *event log* stays debounced (unchanged), since
  those are coarse process signals, not the safety-critical payload.

## 5. MID-FLIGHT UPDATE — "flaky connections are common, not an edge case"

This lands right after the first pass of the draft-persistence implementation
(module + hydrate/persist wiring done, flush-retry not yet reconciled). Revisiting
§2 explicitly:

**Does this change the loss-mode priority?** No — it sharpens it. A had already
won because it subsumes C (an offline gap that outlives the tab IS the total-loss
case). But the update means C-during-open-tab now needs to be a genuinely long
window, not "a blip the retry loop shrugs off in one tick." Re-checked the existing
retry path: `flush()` already re-buffers on `catch` for ANY fetch failure (offline
throws a `TypeError` from `fetch`, so it's already caught, not special-cased) and
the periodic `setInterval(flush, FLUSH_MS)` already retries indefinitely — so a
multi-minute offline stretch with the tab OPEN was already tolerated in memory. The
localStorage layer built for A additionally makes it tolerate the tab being closed
or crashing mid-outage, which is the realistic "hotel wifi + laptop sleeps" story.

**One real gap the update surfaced**: what does "resume" mean if the session id in
the draft is now stale — e.g. a very long offline stretch during which the server
was redeployed/DB reset, or (per Q2) another tab already submitted this draft's
session? Before this update I hadn't handled that: `flush()` would `throw` on any
non-ok response and just re-buffer forever, spinning against a session id that will
never accept the batch again (404) or is already closed (409).

**Q3 asked**: "flaky" — is that mostly the tab staying open (fetches failing/retrying)
or should we plan for candidates closing the laptop and coming back later too?
→ Answer: assume both; laptops sleep through commutes, so plan for "come back
30 minutes later" too, not just "wifi drops for 20 seconds."

**Reconciled**: added explicit 404/409 handling in `flush()` — on either, drop
`sessionIdRef.current` (so the next flush mints a fresh session via the existing
`ensureSession()` lazy-mint path) and keep the batch + files, re-persisting the
draft. This turns a permanently-stuck retry loop into a self-healing one, which is
exactly the "long offline gap, come back later" case Q3 confirmed matters.

- Rejected: a `navigator.sendBeacon` best-effort flush on `visibilitychange`/
  `pagehide`. Sounds appealing for the "closed mid-edit" case, but it only helps
  if the network is up at the moment of closing — on a flaky connection that's
  exactly when it's most likely NOT up, which is the case this update is about.
  localStorage persistence (already built) covers that case unconditionally,
  network state or not, so the beacon would be marginal extra surface for little
  incremental coverage. Flagged as a "would ask the team" item below instead of
  building it blind.

## 6. Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean (schemas:gen + tsc --noEmit, exit 0).
- `node --import ./scripts/test-alias-loader.mjs --experimental-transform-types
  --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test-isolation=process --test
  "app/devcase/apply/*/liveWorkDraft.test.ts"` — 6/6 passing. Covers: round-trip,

  event kinds + non-object files dropped (candidate-writable storage, same
  distrust the server route already applies), and the MAX_FILES/MAX_FILE_BYTES/
  MAX_PENDING_EVENTS caps mirroring the server's own bounds.
- Ran `app/_lib/db/dev-session-paste.test.ts` too (per the task's suggested
  command) to make sure the untouched paste-authenticity path still passes.
  It currently fails in THIS worktree on a `next/server` module-resolution error
  — confirmed pre-existing by `git stash`-ing my changes and re-running: identical
  failure on a clean tree. Not something my change touched or introduced (my
  changes don't import `next/server` anywhere); flagging rather than silently
  ignoring it, since a verifier persona doesn't wave away a red test without
  checking whose fault it is.
- Manual trace of the failure paths my change touches (no dev server in this
  sandboxed pass, so traced against the code, not clicked in a browser):
  - Reload with a saved draft present → `decodeDraft` returns files+pending,
    `setFiles` + `pendingRef` restored, `restored` banner renders, next flush
    reuses the recovered `sessionId`.
  - Reload with `localStorage` disabled/throwing (private mode) → `persistDraft`
    and the read in the mount effect are both wrapped so a throw is swallowed;
    falls back to seed-only behavior identical to pre-change.
  - Flush against a 404'd/409'd session → `sessionIdRef.current` cleared, batch
    re-queued, next `ensureSession()` mints fresh — traced through the code path,
    no infinite-retry-against-a-dead-id branch left.

## 7. What I'd ask the team (not resolved here)

  "we restored your work" notice enough? I kept it flat for scope.
- Is `sendBeacon`-on-unload worth adding as defense-in-depth on top of localStorage,
  given it only helps in the case localStorage already covers unconditionally?
  Leaning no, but it's cheap enough that I'd want the team's steer rather than
  guessing under a timebox.
- Q2's last-write-wins for concurrent tabs/devices: fine for now, but if candidates
  start doing this on purpose (e.g. switching from phone to laptop mid-case), it's
  worth a real "one active session, others read-only" design later.
